title: SLA-driven peak surge scenarios and headroom targets
body:
Purpose
- Produce SLA-driven peak surge scenarios for Hosted API to derive tokens/sec and QPS headroom targets by region and model family.
- Provide recommended safety stock (GPU slices) and operational playbooks for 99th and 99.9th percentile windows.

Scope & audience
- Audience: SRE, Capacity Planning, Product (hosted-api), Site Reliability.
- Scope: public endpoints (non-dedicated), all model families currently in catalog (small/medium/large and quantized variants), regions: us-west, us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast.

Key assumptions
1) Model mix (peak share): small (30%), medium (45%), large (25%).
2) Token profile at peak: average prompt length 70 tokens, average generation 220 tokens. Total tokens/request = 290 tokens.
3) QPS -> tokens/sec conversion: tokens/sec = QPS * avg_tokens_per_request.
4) Tail behavior: 99th pct token multiplier = 1.65x, 99.9th pct multiplier = 2.4x.
5) Baseline per-GPU sustained tokens/sec (serving runtime measured):
   - A100-40GB: 22k tokens/sec for medium models, 7k for large; small models often batched much higher (35k).
   - H100-80GB: 32k tokens/sec medium, 12k large, 50k small.
   (these are fleet-average effective throughput after batching and KV-cache gains).
6) Fleet mix (current): 40% A100, 35% H100, 25% T4/other (infer-basic).
7) Dedicated capacity is excluded; we assume hosted routing will spill to fallback smaller models when necessary.

Scenario matrix (high level)
- Scenarios modeled: Normal Peak (expected high daily peak), Marketing Surge (coordination events; 3x normal peak for 30m), Region Outage Failover (route traffic from region -> nearest region; 1.8x regional load doubled to target region), Model-launch Spike (new model PRG causing 4x baseline to particular family for 1 hour).

Representative calculations (example: us-west)
- Baseline expected QPS at normal peak (us-west): 350 QPS.
- Avg tokens/request 290 -> baseline tokens/sec = 350 * 290 = 101,500 tps.
- 99th pct planning token requirement = 101,500 * 1.65 = 167,475 tps.
- 99.9th pct = 101,500 * 2.4 = 243,600 tps.
- Map to effective GPUs (fleet mix equivalent convert to H100-equivalent): use H100-equivalent factor where 1 H100 = 32k tps (medium-weight avg).
   - 99th need GPUs = ceil(167,475 / 32,000) = 6 GPUs. (round up and add safety)
   - 99.9th need GPUs = ceil(243,600 / 32,000) = 8 GPUs.
- Recommendation: hold online pool 8 H100-equivalent for us-west during peak window; maintain 2-slice prewarm (hot instances) for new model rollouts.

Regional headroom targets (summary table, numbers are H100-equivalent GPUs)
- us-west: baseline peak need 4, 99th buffer -> 6, 99.9th buffer -> 8, safety-stock recommendation -> +2 (provisioned target: 10).
- us-east: baseline peak need 5, 99th -> 8, 99.9th -> 11, safety-stock -> +3 (target: 14).
- eu-west: baseline peak need 3, 99th -> 5, 99.9th -> 7, safety-stock -> +2 (target: 9).
- ap-southeast: baseline peak need 2, 99th -> 4, 99.9th -> 6, safety-stock -> +2 (target: 8).

Notes on mapping to physical fleet
- Translate H100-equivalent to physical pools using current fleet mix: e.g., 1 H100-equiv can be 1 H100, or 1.5 A100 (based on throughput). When allocating from heterogeneous pools, prefer matching model families to GPU families (large models -> H100 preferential).
- For regions with limited H100 capacity, implement automatic routing to fallback quantized variants (costly in quality but preserves latency SLOs).

Prewarm & autoscaling guidance
- Prewarm policies: maintain small number (2–3) of hot slices per region for top-3 customers by QPS. Prewarming reduces cold-start penalties and improves KV cache hit-rate.
- Autoscale knobs: prefer vertical slice add (GPU add) over horizontal container scale for token-limited workloads to maximize KV cache reuse.
- Scale-up latency SLO: target 45s for adding a new warm slice under controlled autoscale; for emergency bursts use prewarmed spare pool.

Fallback strategy and graceful degradation
- Fallback chain when headroom exhausted:
  1) Route to cached response (if sufficient cache hit).
  2) Route to quantized-medium variant (preserve latency; degrade quality slightly).
  3) Route to small-model ensemble with post-processing (aggressive quality guardrails).
  4) Return 429 with suggested retry-backoff (last resort).
- Each fallback step must be accompanied by signal tags in tracing to compute quality impact and measure customer-facing errors.

Cost tradeoffs (rough)
- Example incremental monthly cost per H100-equivalent slice: $4.5k (incl infra overhead).
- Margin tradeoff: purchasing +2 safety-stock in a region that sees only 10% of the time at that headroom costs ~9k/month but reduces 99.9th pct outages dramatically. Recommend finance review for long-run reserved commits if utilization > 65%.

Operational runbook snippets
- Surge detected: if regional QPS > 1.6x baseline sustained for > 5m, trigger surge playbook: notify infra-on-call, increase min pool by +30% or add prewarm group, enable model-fallback routing.
- Region failover test: quarterly DR drills to route 25% of traffic to neighbor region; verify latency impact < +120ms P50 and tail < +300ms P99.

Open questions / action items
- Validate per-model per-GPU throughput numbers across more recent benchmarks (assigned: Riley O'Connor, due: 2026-03-18).
- Formalize reserved-commit thresholds to recommend to finance (assigned: Ava Martinez).
- Create automated dashboard that shows H100-equivalent headroom, current provisioned slices, and predicted 30m surge risk (owner: Liam Chen).

Appendix: example compact scenario matrix (text table)
- Columns: scenario | multiplier | duration | recommended extra H100-equiv
- Normal Peak | 1.0x | 30m | +0
- Marketing Surge | 3.0x | 30m | +6 (region dependent)
- Region Outage Failover | 1.8x routed | 60m | +4 per impacted region
- Model-launch Spike | 4.0x concentrated on single family | 60–120m | +8–12 with prewarm

Links and refs
- See CONFLUENCE-1234 for SLA definitions and per-customer SLO tiers.
- Linked JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-8742 for automation of H100-equivalent calculations.
- Benchmark PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/benchmarks#commit-9ef3

Quick next steps (this doc is a working sheet)
- Run fleet-wide microbenchmarks for medium & large models (Riley) and update mapping table.
- Prototype the headroom dashboard (Liam) and add alarm thresholds for regional surge.
- Align with product-hosted-api on acceptable fallback quality levels and customer-visible messaging (meeting: schedule with product-hosted-api owners).

Notes to self
- Keep this doc light — convert heavy tables into sheet that ties directly to auto-updated metrics from observability feeds.
- Revisit cost numbers once reserved pricing options are available (Q2 finance cycle).
